correctness.rationale: The proof partitions every independent face in the Kronecker cover of a cone into the rim complex, two hub simplices, and the unique edge between hubs. Rim-cover connectivity is witnessed by matched opposite-sheet vertex edges; each cone attaches along a contractible full simplex; the hub edge therefore adds precisely one circle. For a wheel the rim cover is the 2n-cycle or two n-cycles depending on parity. The published cycle theorem gives the complete integer wedge dimensions. Carnero Bravo Theorem 5 supplies the layer-index-three splitting and join-suspension algebra establishes the stated multiplicities, with the zero-index exception explicitly separated. The unique H1 generator is represented by the last hub edge modulo the simply connected rim complex, giving deck sign -1 and rim dihedral sign +1. Exact independently generated mod-two boundary matrices agree for 75 small graphs, 5 wheel covers and six Mycielskians; the all-parameter claim is grounded in the proof, not finite extrapolation. Nontrivial dependence on Theorem 5 is explicitly acknowledged.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 theorem establishes a general recursive homotopy expression but does not compute the wheel input: its examples treat paths, cycles, complete graphs, selected products, forests and grids. The present proof supplies a concrete cone-cover homotopy splitting, its deck action, and evaluated all-layer wheel sphere multiplicities. The 2023 cycle-product paper determines only the rim cover, while earlier generalized-Mycielskian work treats complete graphs. Targeted mathematical record and literature queries and the accessible historical claim set found no equivalent wheel or general coned-cover statement. Indexed search is not a proof of novelty; unindexed equivalences remain a risk.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed wheel evaluation or cone-cover homotopy lemma might imply all or part of the stated theorem.
The published general Mycielskian theorem is essential and covers the formal reduction; the new contribution is an exact structural input and its all-wheel evaluation.
No independent mathematical validation or full cross-index priority search has been performed.

value.rationale: Generalized Mycielskians of a wheel are a natural infinite non-bipartite test family for a 2026 all-graph reduction theorem. A full integral homotopy classification for every rim length and every level order converts the generic conditional formula into explicit binomial sphere multiplicities and dimensions. The universal coned-cover splitting and nontrivial deck sign explain structurally why a 1-sphere appears and is useful beyond wheels. This goes beyond arbitrary small numerical samples or a mere restatement of the published general theorem; the explicit wheel computations were not present in the examined nearest sources. Value is bounded by dependence on existing theory and possible novelty priority risk.
